chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the pilgrim departs from Mina, so he exits from Mecca, and passes the houses of Mecca, then he sleeps, then it becomes morning before he comes to Mina, then there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.بُيُوتَ مَكَّةَ: The houses of Mecca, referring to the residential areas of the city
key_terms.فَلَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: Then there is nothing upon him, meaning no penalty or compensation is required
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Mecca, the holy city containing the Kaaba
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a plain near Mecca where pilgrims spend the nights of Tashriq

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim sleeps in Mecca and misses the night in Mina before dawn?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the flexibility in the Mina residency requirement, establishing that the obligation is to spend the night, not merely to be present at dawn. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of ease (taysir), exempting the pilgrim from the penalty of dam (sacrifice) if the delay in returning was due to necessary travel or rest in Mecca, provided they did not intentionally abandon the rite.
